sections.h2: How does property tax collection work in Islip, NY?
sections.html:
Islip collects through its Receiver of Taxes on a December to May cycle. Collection opens on December 1, bills go out around the second week of December, and the whole year's tax is due on or before January 10. An owner who cannot pay in full can split it, with the first half due January 10 and the second half due May 31.

The town gets only one bill a year onto your doorstep. If a lender escrows your tax, you will not receive the December bill and will get a statement in February after the first half is paid and again in July after the second. A bill that never arrives is no excuse, because state law keeps the owner responsible, and the town cannot waive a penalty.

The 2025-2026 collection ended June 1, 2026. The 2026-2027 tax year begins on December 1, 2026, and the town says details for it will be posted in early to mid December 2026. Taxes become a lien on December 1 of each year. Nobody can pay early, because the Receiver does not know the amount until the warrant arrives from the Suffolk County Legislature.

sections.h2: What does a late Islip property tax payment cost?
sections.html:
Each month after January 10 adds one point of penalty, topping out at 5% for payments made from May 11 to May 31. A partial payment is accepted in person or by mail at any point until May 31, with a minimum of $200 plus any penalty due.

Late penalty schedule, Town of Islip Receiver of Taxes, 2025-2026 collection
Taxes submittedLate penalty
December 1 to January 10None
After January 101%
After February 102%
After March 103%
After April 104%
May 11 to May 315%

Source: Town of Islip, Receiver of Taxes.

Anything unpaid after May 31 moves to the Suffolk County Comptroller at 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, (631) 852-3000, with penalty and interest added. The town's tax office can no longer accept it.

sections.h2: Who sets an Islip assessment, and when is Grievance Day?
sections.html:
The Town Assessor's Office at 40 Nassau Avenue values more than 99,000 parcels and also approves exemptions. The office phone is (631) 224-5585.

Grievance Day follows the Suffolk County pattern of the third Tuesday in May. In 2026 it fell on May 19, with hearing sessions from 9 to 11 am, 2 to 4 pm and 7 to 9 pm, and any complaint that reached the Assessor after 9 pm that day was dismissed as untimely. For the next cycle, the third Tuesday is May 18, 2027, and the tentative roll is finalized on or before May 1. Complaints are hand-delivered to Suite 3 at 40 Nassau Avenue. Board of Assessment Review decisions arrive by regular mail on or about July 1.

  • Informal review: before March 1, the Assessor will look at written proof of value, such as a refinance appraisal dated within a year of July 1 or a nearby arm's-length sale.
  • Assessment estimates: on written request, the office gives a one-year estimate before you add a pool, bathroom or addition.
  • Court review: if the board says no, New York's Small Claims Assessment Review costs $30 for an owner-occupied one to three family home and must start within 30 days of the final roll.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Islip homeowners claim?
sections.html:
Islip handles the Veterans, Senior Citizen, Volunteer Firefighter and Ambulance Worker, Disability, Religious and Not-for-Profit, Home Improvement, Business, First-Time Home Buyer of a Newly Constructed Home and Agricultural exemptions. Every application or renewal is due at the Assessor's Office by March 1.

The Senior Citizen and Persons with Disabilities exemptions use a sliding scale for incomes up to $58,400. The Town Board raised the ceiling in October 2022 from the earlier $37,400. For the 2027/28 year, applications with 2025 income proof are due by March 1, 2027. Seniors apply at Suite 2 (631-224-5058) and persons with disabilities at Suite 3 (631-224-5585).

Basic STAR covers owner-occupied primary homes where the owners and spouses earn less than $250,000, and it removes the first $30,000 of full value from school tax. Enhanced STAR serves owners aged 65 and up with income under $113,550 for 2027/28, and the state will upgrade Basic to Enhanced automatically. For STAR help call the state at 518-457-2036.

sections.h2: What should I know about Islip property tax before selling?
sections.html:
Because tax is a lien from December 1, a sale between December and May needs a payoff for the current year. Ask the Receiver where the bill stands, and then check the title company's search for earlier years.

  • A new owner's name can take up to six months after closing to show on the bill. The December bill follows ownership as of March 1.
  • If the bill shows the word RESTORATION, the prior owner had exemptions the buyer cannot keep, and the buyer repays them once, in that tax year.
  • Owners who finish paying a mortgage should call the Receiver so the records change.
  • The mailing address change form sits in the Forms section of the town site.

A cash buyer can take a house with an open tax balance and pay it from the closing proceeds, which keeps a seller out of the 5% May penalty band. If the house has a senior or disability exemption, tell the buyer early so the restoration amount is not a surprise.

sections.h2: What is Islip like for homeowners and sellers?
sections.html:
Islip is a South Shore town in Suffolk County, incorporated in 1683. It covers 103.2 square miles of land, borders the Atlantic to the south, and includes part of Fire Island, Jones Beach Island and Captree Island. Villages are Brightwaters, Islandia, Ocean Beach and Saltaire, and hamlets include Bay Shore, Brentwood, Central Islip, Sayville, West Islip and Ronkonkoma. Long Island MacArthur Airport, which the town owns, sits in Ronkonkoma, and Fire Island ferries leave from Bay Shore and Sayville.

Water matters to a house here. On August 12 and 13, 2014 the area set a New York record of 13.57 inches of rain in 24 hours, and flooding closed parts of the Southern State Parkway and Sunrise Highway. The town averages about 46 inches of rain a year and 31.8 inches of snow.

QuickFacts for the town reports 340,867 residents in July 2025 and 102,205 households of 3.28 people. Owners occupy 80.5% of homes with a median value of $535,300, and median rent is $2,209. Median household income is $130,132, and 36.6% of residents speak a language other than English at home. The Long Island Rail Road's Montauk Branch serves Bay Shore through Sayville, and the Main Line serves Brentwood, Central Islip and Ronkonkoma.

faqs.q: When does Islip property tax collection start?
faqs.a: Collection for 2026-2027 opens December 1, 2026. Bills are mailed around the second week of December, and the first half is due on or before January 10.

faqs.q: Can I pay Islip property tax early?
faqs.a: No. The Receiver does not know the amounts until the warrant comes from the Suffolk County Legislature in early December.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Islip tax after May 31?
faqs.a: To the Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901. The phone number is (631) 852-3000, and penalty and interest are added.

faqs.q: What is the Islip Grievance Day for 2027?
faqs.a: It is the third Tuesday in May, so May 18, 2027. A complaint must reach the Assessor's Office by 9 pm that day or the Board of Assessment Review dismisses it as untimely.

faqs.q: Why does my Islip bill show the previous owner?
faqs.a: The December bill is built from ownership as of March 1, and a closing after that date can take up to six months to show in the system. The new owner still owes the tax.
